decisions.executionNote: Raise and bend both arms elbow-up toward their own support blocks; initial conservative approach before visual alignment.
Align open grippers with the inner left and right white supports, using separate workspace approaches and small orientation corrections.
Fine-align with the visible block axes, descend slightly, and close both grippers. Retention will be checked on lifting.
Lift both supports clear and align their axes while moving toward symmetric base positions. Keep closed and check RGB for retention and depth alignment.
Lower both retained supports back to table height at symmetric positions and release gently; next retreat will expose the base alignment.
Withdraw open jaws upward and outward from the two base supports, then begin turning for a coordinated end grasp of the long board.
Complete mirrored end-grasp orientation above the long board. The two upright base supports are visible; a small fore-aft difference remains within the board footprint.
Approach the long board symmetrically from both ends and close the jaws at grasp height. Lift only after checking alignment.
Maintain fully closed commands to seat the board grasp, then lift both ends equally for a visual retention check.
Carry the visibly retained long board level over the two base supports, then begin a slow centered descent.
Settle the lower board onto both upright supports, open both grippers, and start withdrawing without disturbing the centered layer.
Leave the stable lower layer untouched and approach the remaining side blocks with open jaws, rotating back toward upright-block grasps.
Align with the remaining blocks' visible yaw and approach above their sides. Keep jaws open and leave descent margin for wrist-image refinement.
Refine yaw from wrist views and descend to grasp height with open jaws; pause to verify centering before closure.
Center both white blocks between the fingers using wrist-image offsets, make the final shallow descent, and close for a retention test.
Lift both closed grasps above the lower board, straighten the held supports upright, and start carrying inward while checking visual retention.
Carry the retained upright blocks to symmetric middle-support positions above the completed lower board, maintaining height and closed jaws.
Lower the two upright middle supports evenly toward the lower board, retaining a small final settling margin before release.
Finish a shallow settling descent, release the middle supports, and withdraw open jaws upward to expose and verify their stability.
Withdraw from the upright middle supports and turn both open grippers toward the ends of the shorter board at the front of the table.
Finish mirrored board-grasp orientations and descend symmetrically toward the short board's ends, leaving a final height margin.
Complete the final descent at both ends of the short board and close symmetrically, pausing before the lift.
Seat both closed grasps, then lift the short board level above table height and check retention before moving over the tower.
Carry the visibly retained short board level above the middle supports, adding clearance before centering over the lower layer.
Lower the centered short board evenly onto the two upright middle supports, keeping both ends level and closed until the settling check.
Settle the middle board the final few millimeters, open both jaws, and withdraw upward/outward to check that the layer remains centered and stable.
Move clear of the stable middle layer toward the two remaining top pieces. Left approaches the green cap from outside; right turns to grasp the small wooden board along its current axis.
Approach the cap and small board with open jaws, correcting the cap's lateral wrist-image offset and finishing the board's approach orientation before final grasp refinement.
Use wrist images for shallow final alignment: center the cap between the left fingers and the small board between the right fingers; keep open pending a close-range check.
Make small in-plane seating corrections at both top pieces and close the centered jaws. Hold still before checking retention with a lift.
Lift both closed top-piece grasps well clear of the table, straighten the cap's yaw, and begin turning the small board horizontally while checking retention.
Bring the small board above the tower center while completing its horizontal alignment. Keep the retained cap waiting safely to the left, without crossing arms.
Lower the centered small board gently onto the middle layer while the left arm holds the cap safely aside; keep the right jaws closed until contact is checked.
Release the small centered board and withdraw the right gripper upward and to its own side, leaving the cap held stationary until the placement is exposed.
Move the retained cap above the small centered board. Withdraw the empty right arm toward its home side with a continuous elbow-up rotation.
Center and gently lower the upright cap toward its small board. Continue returning the empty right arm toward origin without disturbing the tower.
Settle the cap onto the small top board and open the left jaws without lateral disturbance. Finish the right arm's return to origin.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward and away from the released cap, then start returning toward origin while checking that the full tower remains stable.
Return the empty left arm toward its origin with open jaws and continuous elbow-up configuration. The completed tower is visibly standing centered.
